# Forecasting {.hero #s09-forecasting}

::: {.sem-mark data-sem="9"}
Seminar 9 · Exponential smoothing
:::

$\alpha$ is how much you trust the latest number.

::: {.lede}
$F_{t+1} = \alpha x_t + (1-\alpha)F_t$ uses the latest observation and the previous forecast. Expanding the recursion shows that it includes all past observations, with decreasing weights for older values.
:::

## Weights in exponential smoothing {.stage-slide #smooth-intuition}

::: {.stage-wrap .stage-wrap-std}
<div id="smooth-stage" class="stage"></div>
:::

[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="smooth-frag-1"}
[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="smooth-frag-2"}

::: {.slide-footer}
At $\alpha = 0.8$, the forecast closely follows the previous month's value. At $\alpha = 0.2$, it is smoother and responds more slowly to changes. Choose $\alpha$ according to the response required.
:::

## Choosing $\alpha$ using forecast errors {.sim-slide #smooth-sim}

::: {.slide-kicker}
Seminar 9 · MSE and MAE
:::

::: {.lede-min}
This series trends upward, violating the assumption of no trend. Starting with $F_2 = 67$, calculate the forecast errors for each value of $\alpha$.
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-text}
```{webr-r}
x <- c(45, 62, 73, 87, 86, 95)   # <-- trending
err <- function(a) {
  f <- 67
  for (k in 2:5) f[k] <- a*x[k] + (1-a)*f[k-1]
  x[2:6] - f[1:5] }
for (a in c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)) {
  e <- err(a)
  cat("a", a, " MSE", round(mean(e^2), 1),
      " MAE", round(mean(abs(e)), 2), "\n") }
```
:::

::: {.try-this}
Both error metrics decrease as $\alpha$ increases. After the first month, every error is positive because the forecast lags behind the upward trend. Persistent errors of the same sign indicate the need for a model that includes a trend.
:::
